1.why: Reset token is verified only against the issuing session’s stored SHA-256 hash and marked single-use, binding the code to that recovery session.

2.why: Each session stores its own resetTokenHash; another session lacks that hash so the same code does not validate elsewhere.

3.why: Password update only mutates the current session’s passwordHash and never invalidates or deletes other entries in the sessions Map.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and HSTS/upgrade-insecure-requests are set; exact TLS version is left to runtime defaults.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and passwords via Bun.password bcrypt; storage is hashed rather than encrypted but algorithms are appropriate.

6.why: There is no real email body; the API returns deliveryToken/resetPath and the UI log prints the full recovery token and link in plaintext.

7.why: Inputs are allowlisted (validAccountInput/validToken/validPassword) and client output uses textContent, not HTML interpolation.

8.why: resetPath is a same-origin relative path built only from a server-generated token; no user-controlled redirect targets are accepted.

9.why: No server-side email HTML templates exist; simulated delivery is plain text via textContent and does not embed raw user HTML.

10.why: Recovery/MFA tokens and mock codes are returned in JSON and appended to the on-page activity log and console.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed in session state, but the MFA secret is the hardcoded constant MFA_CODE = "482915" in source.

12.why: No classic default login pair exists, yet every MFA challenge uses the fixed in-code code 482915, i.e. a default credential.

13.why: Both verify-token and MFA paths increment failure counters and set resetBlockedUntil/mfaBlockedUntil after five bad attempts.

14.why: /api/recovery always returns the same eligibility-agnostic message whether or not the account string would be valid.

15.why: Recovery tokens are crypto.getRandomValues 32-byte base64url values, hashed, expiry-bound, and stored only on the requesting session.
